question: When will the Commission provide real support for agriculture across the EU by implementing the following measures: 1.
uniformly applying the principles of food equality, food stability and food security;
closing the gap between farmers in western Europe (high subsidies and low interest rates on credit) and farmers in eastern Europe (low subsidies and high interest rates on credit);
protecting these key assets that the European Union currently has at its disposal (farming and beekeeping) and securing the European Union’s food future?
answer: 1. The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plans (CSP) are the key tool to deliver on the objectives of the CAP, including food security and food stability. It provides EUR 307 billion in public expenditure between 2023 and 2027. It contributes to economic objectives, environmental and climate objectives as well as social objectives.

In addition, other horizontal and sectoral EU legislation set out harmonised rules for the placing on the market of food and food-related inputs ensuring a high level of protection of food safety across the EU. 2. All regions in the EU come from a different starting point.

For direct payments, the CAP’s main income support tool, average subsidy levels are converging since 2014 and will continue to converge until 2027, as agreed in the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2021-2027. 3. As under point 1, the CSPs are the key tool to strengthen the key assets of sustainable farming in the EU.

More specifically, the amount made available for beekeeping increased by 50% to EUR 60 million per year in the current MFF. The non-authorisation of certain plant protection products that were considered detrimental to bees also supports protecting beekeeping.
